## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Duṭṭhullavācā-sikkhāpada* ("Indecent speech", Bu-Vb Ss 3) is the third training rule of the *Saṅghādisesa* section in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Vinaya Piṭaka. The disciplinary rule mandates that a monk overcome by lust who speaks to a woman using sexually explicit or indecent language incurs a grave offense requiring formal suspension and rehabilitation by the Saṅgha. An English translation of the rule has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
